name: Tennessee cotton-ginning service
description: By March 1801 Andrew Jackson owned a cotton gin and processed cotton for nearby farmers in the Nashville area, according to a historical buildings report.

date.label: By March 1801
date.basis: The historical report describes ownership and service by March 1801; the start is unknown.

events.statement: By March 1801 Andrew Jackson owned a cotton gin and processed cotton for nearby farmers in the Nashville area, according to a historical buildings report.

evidence.supports: The report cites a March 1801 receipt and describes Jackson processing neighbors’ cotton.
The Library of Congress discusses enslaved labor in cotton work and older ginning forms; it does not identify this gin’s workers.

events.caveats: The report does not locate the particular 1801 machine precisely or identify its operators. Enslaved labor underpinned the region’s plantation economy; no unnamed individual is assigned to this specific gin.

contributions.resource: Owner of gin and service arrangement; operator not identified
